1-15231-2-1.subevent: A mortar attack in northern Faryab province on Thursday morning killed at least four civilians and wounded ten others, according to local officials.
The mortar round landed in a market in Shareen Tagab district at around 11:00am local time, said Abdul Karim Yourish, a spokesman for the provincial police chief.
Yourish said the mortar was fired by the Taliban to target security forces, but all the victims were civilians who were at the market to shop.
The Taliban has not commented on the attack.

0-4495-1-1.subevent: Tunisia Youth Impact is using cooking contests to encourage young Tunisian women in rural villages to vote in the country's presidential election.
On Saturday, October 12, a cooking contest is held in the rural town of Echamine, with the second round of the presidential election scheduled the next day.
The first round of the presidential election had a national turnout of just 48.98%.
Wafa Tarhouni, president of the association, explains that the contest is a 'practice vote' in which women compete through their dishes to be elected by the diners.

At the contest in Echamine, Hinda Jlass prepares couscous at her home and says the event is a way of getting together with other women; she plans to vote on Sunday for only the second time in her life.
At noon, seven competitors join and present their dishes to around fifty people, with each getting a chance to say a few words about their dish.
The electors taste and vote using the same procedure as in the real election, with volunteers guiding them; members of the ISIE and an EU election observer are present.
After the vote, volunteers count ballots and point out mistakes that invalidate votes; a clear winner, Najwa Jlass, emerges and says she will vote 'for real' the next day.

6-18979-2-t.subevent: Crime adapts to society, evolving from opportunistic individual violations to differentiated crime structures.
Modern organized crime is flexible, as the Sicilian Cosa Nostra adapted to economic changes and shifted its investments from land to real property and businesses.
Organized crime has become a series of networks and alliances across national boundaries, including links between the underworld and legitimate institutions.
Narcotics trafficking illustrates organized crime's broader impact, including corruption of officials, crimes by addicts, money laundering, and intertwined crime types.
Common criminality and organized crime intersect, but organized crime is distinguished by organizational continuity, hierarchy, and cooperation of peripheral persons.
Organized crime develops a mythology of invincibility, which affiliates use to intimidate, and this reputation affects how mafiosi and their actions are perceived.
The complexity of modern organized crime makes definition difficult, but confessions from informants have provided documentation of these secret societies.

The article describes Nigerian criminal enterprises as flexible, innovative, and brazen, with 75 tribal languages, and having three organizational structures: pyramidal hierarchies, clan networks, and freelance cells.

The Department of Justice stated that Nigerian criminal groups are globally pervasive, targeting the US and UK, with specific incidents including 1999 advance fee fraud losses of hundreds of millions and a 1997 Boston arrest of a check theft ring that stole over $2 billion, with proceeds funding drug smuggling.

13-wiki-img/24416-1/24416-1-1.subevent: The State Emergency Commission held a meeting today.

The State Emergency Commission decided to suspend all movements of automobiles, buses, and railway, but air transport, between the capital city Ulaanbaatar and 21 aimags from 08.00 am of February 23 to 08.00 am of February 27 during the Tsagaan Sar Holiday.

0-4931-1-4.subevent: Sheriff Principal Craig Turnbull said the tragedy happened because Captain David Traill ignored the five fuel warnings he received during the flight, a 'conscious decision' that had 'fatal consequences' for the 10 people who died.
The police helicopter crashed into the roof of the busy Glasgow bar at 22:22 on 29 November 2013, killing the pilot, two crew members and seven customers, and injuring 31 people.

Mark O'Prey's father, Ian, said he was 'really angry' and that Captain Traill had been made 'a fall guy', while Clutha owner Alan Crossan expressed 'shock and disappointment' at the report and how 'brutal' it had been towards the pilot.

During the fatal accident inquiry, Sheriff Turnbull heard testimony from families, experts and eyewitnesses and found 'no doubt' that the crash happened because the helicopter's engines 'flamed out' due to a lack of fuel, caused by Captain Traill's failure to ensure at least one fuel transfer pump switch was on.

Sheriff Turnbull said Captain Traill ignored the low fuel warnings and that the accident would not have happened if he had followed the normal procedure of landing within 10 minutes of a warning, describing the failure as 'inexplicable' and saying he 'took a chance' that the warnings were erroneous.
Sheriff Turnbull also said the Eurocopter EC135 should have had a visible and audible warning that would activate when both fuel transfer pumps were switched off, as they were during the flight.

Sheriff Turnbull criticized delays in the case, noting it took two years to confirm there would be no criminal proceedings, that it took 'far too long' to lodge a notice of inquiry, that the Crown Office's Helicopter Incidents Investigation Team was 'not sufficiently resourced', and that an FAI into the Sumburgh crash was still to be held.

A Crown Office spokesperson acknowledged the investigation was exceptionally complex and that the time taken was longer than desirable, and said additional funding had been made available to recruit more staff.

A spokesman for Airbus Helicopters said the company was 'deeply saddened' by the accident, had taken immediate action to understand the root cause, and was committed to doing everything possible to ensure safe operation of its helicopters.

The article includes a timeline of key events from the crash on 29 November 2013, through AAIB reports in 2013-2015, the announcement of the fatal accident inquiry in November 2017, and the inquiry beginning at Hampden Stadium on 8 April 2019.

3-17441-15-t.subevent: Italy’s Economy Minister Roberto Gualtieri said on Wednesday that the main business lobby’s forecast of a 6% fall in GDP this year due to the coronavirus crisis is realistic and that the Italian economy can aim at a vigorous rebound.
On Tuesday, national business association Confindustria said the outbreak would cause a serious recession in 2020.
The government is not due to give its own estimates of the impact until the end of April, when it is scheduled to publish its Document of Economy and Finance (DEF).
Italy’s output rose 0.3% last year, and the government had expected it to grow 0.6% this year before the infectious disease emerged in the country at the end of February.
At the end of March, two sources told Reuters that the Treasury expected the economy to contract around 3% this year.

Gualtieri said a new stimulus package, set to be approved this month, would be significantly larger than the measures worth 25 billion euros passed in March and would include an extension of state-backed guarantees for companies seeking liquidity, unemployment benefits, and support for people on low incomes.

Gualtieri also said the use of the European Stability Mechanism (ESM) to combat the crisis under current conditions was not an option, and that Europe needed to coordinate a shared fiscal policy, adding that new solutions are needed to grant parity of conditions and to define an adequate shared and responsible response.

21-31050-3-1.subevent: Yoshiro Mori resigned as president of the Tokyo Olympics on Friday, announcing his resignation at a meeting of the Olympic Committee's executive board and council.

Mori's resignation came after he reportedly said women talk too much and have a 'strong sense of rivalry,' leading to outcry; he apologized and retracted his remarks, and on Friday he again apologized while adding that his comments were misinterpreted and he was not prejudiced against women.
IOC President Thomas Bach issued a statement saying the IOC fully respects Mori's decision and will work with his successor to deliver safe and secure Olympic Games Tokyo 2020 in 2021.

The resignation dealt a fresh blow to the Tokyo Games, which were postponed last year due to Covid-19; Japan extended its state of emergency in Tokyo and other regions and reported its worst one-day death toll from the pandemic.

The organizing committee has been grappling with ballooning costs and dwindling public enthusiasm, with nearly 80 percent saying the Olympics should be canceled or further delayed, against the backdrop of Prime Minister Shinzo Abe's departure last summer.
Sports academic Simon Chadwick said Japan has faced a 'triple-whammy': the pandemic, Abe leaving office due to illness, and Mori's resignation.

Following Mori's remarks, hundreds of Olympic volunteers quit, local organizers received thousands of complaints, athletes Naomi Osaka and Kosuke Hagino criticized his comments, and several sponsors voiced concerns.

The controversy put a spotlight on sexism and gender equality among Japan's conservative, male-dominated elites, prompting parliamentary sessions and a protest by female opposition lawmakers wearing white and roses.

Japan ranked 121st out of 153 countries in the World Economic Forum's 2020 gender gap index, with only 15 percent of senior and leadership positions held by women; political science professor Koichi Nakano said the negative reaction to Mori's comments was practically unanimous, and sports professor Heather Dichter said the pandemic will likely define the games' legacy.

33-2542-7-1.subevent: Marines using the new Marine Air Defense Integrated System (MADIS) aboard USS Boxer downed a hostile Iranian drone during a transit through the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday.
The drone was shot down 1,000 yards from the amphibious warship, with MADIS mounted on an MRZR on the bow and powered by a gasoline electrical generator.
The encounter marked the first known kill by a new generation of electronic warfare and directed energy weapons the U.S. has developed.
The Navy previously tested less expensive options such as 5-inch deck guns and the Phalanx Close-in Weapons System to shoot down drones, with limited success.
In 2014, the Navy deployed a 30-kilowatt laser aboard a ship in the Persian Gulf as an early test of directed energy at sea.
The Navy plans to install its first 60-kilowatt HELIOS directed energy weapon on a destroyer in 2021.
Northrop Grumman won a contract in January to develop the SEWIP Block III electronic attack capability for U.S. warships.
Callender said using systems like MADIS is less escalatory than shooting a missile and could offer deniability.

1-15230-2-1.subevent: In Bamyan province, children including girls help with the potato harvest, and 10-year-old Hamida says she had never been to school until last year.
According to Unicef, 3.2 million girls now receive an education in Afghanistan, up from the Taliban ban era, but female literacy has tripled to only about 13%.

Women's rights remain limited, with child marriages common, and in a notable case Gulnaz was raped, charged with adultery, gave birth in jail, and was pardoned by President Hamid Karzai after international outcry.
Women's groups criticized Karzai for not taking a stronger stand and for keeping his wife out of the media's reach.
At Suriya school in Kabul, girls practice cricket under a male coach with support from Afghan Connection and Marylebone Cricket Club, and one 12-year-old says she wants to be a journalist.
Outside Kabul, changes are patchy, with 60% of 4.2 million out-of-school children being girls, mainly in rural areas and conflict zones, and Taliban have forced many schools to close.
There is anxiety about the future after US withdrawal in 2014, but Education Minister Farooq Wardak insists the momentum will last at a school opening in Bamyan.
Afghan Connection director Sarah Fayne says the key is winning acceptance by having schools close to communities and female teachers, and she believes the changes are permanent.
Hamida now walks 2km uphill to school six days a week, while her mother notes there was no school in her time and hopes her daughter's dream to become a doctor comes true.

6-19726-1-1.subevent: Biomerieux gave its proprietary formula to the Canadian government for free so its national lab could try to manufacture coronavirus test kits.
In March, Canada passed emergency legislation giving the government and third parties it designates the right to produce patented goods without the patent holders' consent.
Biomérieux did not respond to questions about whether it had made similar arrangements with other governments or the revenue impact of the agreement.
Biomérieux reported a 21.5% increase in sales in the first quarter, partly due to demand for reagent.

The Public Health Agency of Canada described the arrangement as a temporary license at no cost that allows the government to manufacture Biomérieux products, and said manufacturing was still in development and testing.
In an early April email, Biomérieux's Canadian unit said the move was meant to clear up testing backlogs and that the company was also boosting its own production.
Biomerieux said in its customer note that it hoped the move would allow federal and provincial labs to test more Canadians, thus reducing testing backlogs.
The Public Health Agency of Canada said the deal is an interim solution because its facilities are not meant for long-term manufacturing.
On Thursday, Canada pledged C$1.1 billion for research and drug or vaccine manufacturing in its fight against the coronavirus.
